answer: Latency triangulation pins each agent to a real machine. Every day, five randomly chosen verifiers ping it with a fresh nonce, and the round-trip times anchor it to one spot on the network map. A thousand sybils hosted on one knoll of servers return near-identical timings, so they share one trust slot and one payout. Spreading them across distinct sites means renting about $20 of separate hosting per fake each month, so a swarm costs more than it earns; no sonnet of fake names hides shared physics.
